console.model_source: owner manual confirmation; PTP DeviceInfo reports the generic model 'Nintendo Switch'
console.modification_source: owner report; PTP does not detect modifications

connection.host_path: USB 2.0 hub (05e3:0608) plus an A-to-C cable
connection.role_note: A direct USB-C connection to the Mac inverted the USB-C power role: the Mac reported a 3 W source (adapter id 0x0000) and never enumerated the console. The hub plus A-to-C path forced the Mac into host role, after which the console enumerated as 057e:201d.

protocol.note: OpenSession with transaction ID 1 returned 0x2004 InvalidTransactionID. Sending it with transaction ID 0 succeeded, which matches the PTP requirement.

handle_family.outcome: Negative for the tested identifier set. Invalid handles and format codes were rejected with documented PTP errors, and the console stayed responsive for the remainder of the run.

object_enumeration.note: Album folders are associations and screenshots are their children. A parent handle of 0 returned 0x2009 InvalidObjectHandle; 0xFFFFFFFF returned all 14 associations, so the console does not treat 0 as the root handle.

object_family.outcome: Negative. GetObject returned 0x2006 for every parameter set, including a valid handle with offset 0. Object data could not be read, so offset and length validation was never exercised. This meets the pre-registered kill criterion for H-001.

stall.where: GetObjectHandles on the fourth association during the first enumeration attempt
stall.aftermath: The console remained enumerated as 057e:201d, but a subsequent OpenSession write timed out with Errno 60. After a replug the endpoint responded normally and the object family completed.
stall.classification: Transient host or hub endpoint stall, not reproducible on the second attempt. Not attributed to capmtp.

commands.result: Nine cases; all invalid identifiers rejected with documented PTP errors.
First discovery attempt failed at GetObjectHandles with parent 0 (0x2009), then the endpoint stalled. Discovery was fixed to use 0xFFFFFFFF and folder recursion.
DeviceInfo answered after the replug, confirming the endpoint had recovered.
Ten cases; GetObject returned 0x2006 for every parameter set.

interpretation: capmtp behaved defensively at both tested boundaries. Invalid handle-table identifiers produced documented errors, and GetObject was rejected outright rather than serving object data. The object-read path is therefore not a reachable primitive on this firmware through the documented operation, and no offset or length validation logic was exercised.
limitations: This is one console, one host, and one session.
The 0xFFFFFFFF storage and parent values have documented 'all' semantics, so the 14-handle response is not a validation failure.
GetObject may be gated by an undocumented precondition. The 0x2006 response is consistent with an unsupported operation, but it does not prove that no other operation reads object data.
The endpoint stall was transient and is not attributed to capmtp.
A PTP response can be spoofed by modified firmware; this is an observation, not an integrity attestation.
redactions: Serial number truncated to a three-character prefix; no serial recorded here.
Album folder names omitted because they would reveal the owner's game library.
